name: Cao Lan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Gregerson, Kenneth & Edmondson, Jerold A. 1998 (phonological study of Cao Lan, cited on Glottolog caol1238); not found online

sources.citation: Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten (eds.), A Survey of Word Accentual Patterns in the Languages of the World, ch.10. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Cao Lan appears only in the Tai-Kadai classification list (p.596); the family-level 'Accent information' (p.598) gives data for Thai and Lao only ('All languages in this family are tonal and morphemes are monosyllabic'); nothing specific to Cao Lan.

sources.citation: Phan Lương Hùng. 2012. Vị trí của tiếng Cao Lan trong các ngôn ngữ Tai [The position of Cao Lan among the Tai languages]. Tạp chí Ngôn ngữ 2012(8): 69-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States (first page) 'Tiếng Cao Lan là một ngôn ngữ đơn tiết, có thanh điệu' (Cao Lan is a monosyllabic, tonal language); lexicostatistics and shared innovations; notes that the only synchronic description is the author's own 2010 MA thesis 'Ngữ âm tiếng Cao Lan' (ref. 8b).

sources.citation: Nguyễn Văn Lợi. 2004. Quan hệ Cao Lan, Sán Chí xét về mặt ngôn ngữ [The Cao Lan – Sán Chí relationship from a linguistic point of view]. Tạp chí Dân tộc học 2004(3): 48-60.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives the Cao Lan tone system from the 2003 Institute of Linguistics survey (A1 44, A2 32, B 32, C1 35, C2 454, DS 44/32, DL 32) and sound-change diagnostics; mentions tone sandhi-like 'biến thanh trong ngữ lưu' as a Chinese-contact feature, no accent statement. (PDF text is TCVN3-encoded; converted copy.)

sources.citation: Gregerson, Kenneth J. & Jerold A. Edmondson. 1998. Some puzzles in Cao Lan. In Somsonge Burusphat (ed.), The International Conference on Tai Studies, 151-163. Bangkok: Institute of Language and Culture for Rural Development, Mahidol University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Tonal system' (pp.153-158) reports a collapsed Tai tone system (pitch distinguishes only ~3 categories in live syllables, 2 in checked: 31, 42, 35; 45, 34), partly compensated by tense/lax voice and vowel-quality differences; sec. 4 is on initial-cluster reflexes and lexicon. No mention of stress/accent anywhere in the 13 pages (read in full as page images; scan has no text layer).

sources.citation: Strecker, David. 1985. The classification of the Caolan languages. In S. Ratanakul, D. Thomas & S. Premsrirat (eds.), Southeast Asian Linguistic Studies Presented to André-G. Haudricourt, 479-492. Bangkok: Mahidol University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; historical-comparative argument (reflexes of *tr-, *dl-, tone of 'rice') that Caolan, Ts'un-wa and Nung-an are ?Yai (Northern Tai). Read in full.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, André-G. 1960. Note sur les dialectes de la région de Moncay. Bulletin de l'École française d'Extrême-Orient 50(1): 161-177 (repr. in Haudricourt 1972, Problèmes de phonologie diachronique, 209-233).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Earliest linguistic treatment of Cao Lan / Ts'un-wa / Nung-an with tone notation; open on Persée but the PDF sits behind an anti-bot challenge by automated download; should be checked for any remark on accent.

sources.citation: Bonifacy, A. 1907. Étude sur les Cao Lan. T'oung Pao sér. II, 8: 429-438.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; wordlist with tone marks in quốc-ngữ-style transcription, a paragraph on consonant/vowel correspondences and one on syntax.

sources.citation: Viện Ngôn ngữ học (Nguyễn Văn Lợi et al.). 2003-2004. Field survey report on Cao Lan and Sán Chí (Quảng Ninh, Bắc Giang, Tuyên Quang, Thái Nguyên), presented at Hội thảo Xác định thành phần dân tộc Sán Chay (Cao Lan - Sán Chỉ), Viện Ngôn ngữ học - Viện Dân tộc học, Bắc Giang 2004.

sources.note: Underlying survey whose stated aim no.1 was to establish the phonological ('cấu trúc ngữ âm'), grammatical and lexical structure of Cao Lan; the published 2004 article gives only the tone table.

sources.citation: Phan Lương Hùng. 2011. Cao Lan Tones. [Conference paper, probably SEALS XXI, Kasetsart University, Bangkok, May 2011.] Semantic Scholar CorpusId 114481408.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Dedicated instrumental/descriptive study of Cao Lan tone by the same fieldworker; may contain remarks on prosodic word structure and stress in sesquisyllables/compounds.

sources.citation: Phan Lương Hùng. 2010. Ngữ âm tiếng Cao Lan [Phonetics of the Cao Lan language]. Luận văn Thạc sĩ Ngôn ngữ học, Trường Đại học Khoa học Xã hội và Nhân văn, Đại học Quốc gia Hà Nội.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only systematic synchronic phonological description of Cao Lan (so described by its author in Tạp chí Ngôn ngữ 2012/8); a Vietnamese 'ngữ âm' thesis normally has an explicit syllable-structure/thanh điệu chapter and would be the place where any statement on trọng âm (stress) in disyllables/compounds appears.
